title: Provider Ecosystem and Federated Knowledge
objective: Scale provider coverage through manifests, native adapters, signed knowledge bundles, and explicit trust promotion.

stories.title: Manifest schema v1
stories.outcome: Define declarative roots/artifact patterns/capability hints that are inspection-safe by default.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest-only integrations cannot acquire destructive capability implicitly.
Schema is versioned and rejects unknown security-relevant fields.

stories.title: Signed knowledge bundle format
stories.outcome: Package provider/version/layout intelligence separately from the binary with signature/provenance verification.
acceptance_criteria: Unsigned/invalid bundles are ignored with diagnostics.
Knowledge update cannot raise authority beyond local trust policy.
Rollback to prior trusted bundle is supported.
verification: Tamper, rollback, expiry, and unknown-signer tests.

stories.title: Gemini CLI adapter
stories.outcome: Add discovery/inventory first, then only capabilities supported by verified evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter starts at truthful capability subset.
Vendor-native retention is detected/explained where relevant.
verification: Provider conformance suite and version fixtures.

stories.title: GitHub Copilot CLI adapter
stories.outcome: Add local session/state inventory with capability truthfulness.
acceptance_criteria: SQLite/internal state is not mutated without documented native capability.

stories.title: OpenCode adapter
stories.outcome: Add local state inventory and cleanup capabilities incrementally.
acceptance_criteria: Community contribution path exercises same trust pipeline.

stories.title: Community provider verification workflow
stories.outcome: Automate manifest lint, fixture tests, trust-level labeling, and maintainer promotion criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Community PR cannot mark itself Built-in Verified.
Promotion requires maintainer-owned evidence and compatibility tests.

stories.title: The knowledge-bundle verifier compiles on the promised toolchain
stories.outcome: E16-S02 wrote three let-chains in the bundle verifier. Let-chains are stable from Rust 1.88 and this workspace promises 1.85.0 (ADR-0015), so the MSRV leg of rust.yml has been unable to compile cancellai-safety since 2026-09-09 - through v1.12.0 and v1.13.0, both of which failed to publish for other reasons that masked this one. Fixing the dependency side of the MSRV break (E09-S05) removed the error that stopped cargo before it compiled anything, and this one appeared underneath it. The conditions are rewritten with `is_some_and`, which is stable well below the promised version, leaving the promise intact rather than renegotiating it. Raising the MSRV is the alternative and is an owner decision about a published compatibility promise, not an executor's.
acceptance_criteria: The rewritten conditions shall accept and reject exactly what the let-chains did.
If a bundle's expiry time has been reached exactly, then verification shall reject it, and rollback shall refuse to reinstate it.
If a bundle carries no expiry, then it shall not be treated as expired.
A bundle from a publisher other than the current one shall not be refused as stale on sequence alone.
The workspace shall compile on the promised minimum toolchain on all three tier-1 platforms.
verification: The boundary is pinned in both places the comparison appears: verification already had it, rollback did not and now does.
The different-publisher case is covered by an existing test that applies a lower sequence from a second publisher over a current bundle and expects it to succeed.
The MSRV legs of rust.yml are the only proof available here that 1.85 compiles: no 1.85 toolchain is installed on the executor's machine, and installing one is not an executor decision.
